About me

I have over 10 years of experience in digital marketing, CRM, and Content Operations. In addition to leading content teams as a Technical Lead, I have worked on mapping and building processes, frameworks, knowledge bases, and automations that helped content and QA teams operate with greater quality, consistency, and efficiency.

Case 01
Writing QA & Editorial Governance System
Challenge
The content creation process relied heavily on manual reviews and consultations across multiple support documents, making the writing stage more time-consuming and error-prone. As the operation grew, greater editorial consistency and faster approval cycles became increasingly necessary.
Solution
I designed a validation system directly within the content production tool, using automated Correction, Attention, and Standardization messages based on predefined content quality criteria. Brand guidelines, business rules, and platform requirements were translated into a scalable and repeatable validation workflow. The project consolidated editorial best practices, reduced subjective decision-making, and created a more predictable process for content writers, QA reviewers, and managers.
❌ Alert: Email subject line ending with a period automatically detected
❌ Alert: Card title exceeded the 30-character limit
Results
  • Greater editorial consistency across content pieces
  • Reduced rework during later production stages
  • Improved efficiency in the approval process
  • Centralized editorial knowledge within a single reference structure
Case 02
Content Automation at Scale
Context
A CRM operation produced segmented campaigns for different audiences, regions, and Beauty Consultant profiles. Each campaign could generate dozens of variations, requiring the creation and review of hundreds of Airtable records.
Challenge
A significant portion of the information was identical across campaign variations but still needed to be manually entered into every record. This created a high operational workload, constant rework, increased risk of inconsistencies, and longer writing, review, and approval cycles.
Solution
I redesigned the Airtable operational architecture by creating an intermediary layer to centralize content shared across all campaign versions. Repeated information began to be entered only once and distributed automatically. Manual fields were replaced by formulas and automation rules, simplifying the workflow for both Content and QA teams.
Pre-Personalization Table: Shared fields registered once — Constraints, Template, and Product Type automatically distributed.
Main Personalization Table: Previously manual fields automatically inherited through Lookup fields — Campaign, Type, Brand, Constraints, Template, and more.
Impact
  • Significant reduction in manual work
  • Lower incidence of operational errors
  • Faster campaign creation and review cycles
  • More scalable structure for high-volume operations
  • Centralized maintenance of content and business rules
Case 03
Scalable Content Architecture — Template Library
Challenge
As content volume increased, challenges emerged around standardization, knowledge reuse, and production speed. Information and references were scattered across documents, spreadsheets, and teams, with no centralized source of truth.
Solution
I developed a modular knowledge system organized into three levels: Content Atoms (reusable components), Content Blocks (functional combinations of those components), and Templates (complete production structures). The system consolidated reusable models and operational references within a single architecture. The initiative accelerated content production for complex, high-volume projects, improved onboarding for new writers, and strengthened operational governance.
Module Library Overview: Category-based navigation, template filtering, and structured Content and Notes columns.
Content Column: Replicable content framework including text structure, variations, and dynamic fields.
Notes Column: Usage instructions, campaign examples, and completion guidelines.
Results
  • Faster content creation
  • Reduced effort when starting new projects
  • Standardization of formats and best practices
  • Improved knowledge sharing across teams
  • Easier onboarding for new writers
